assertions.name: the_obstruction_is_located_in_the_quark_block
assertions.source: core 6 is EVEN and the quark block 3 is ODD for both nucleons, so the core contributes nothing to the parity and the whole question reduces to the gluon dressing. This is what makes the result a budget statement rather than a claim about one word

assertions.name: nine_and_eleven_have_the_same_parity_so_neither_helps
assertions.source: build_nucleon_nf emits 9 (B_3 IS the gluon structure, per its own docstring) and the live nucleon_word_letters emits 11. They differ by 2, so they share a parity and BOTH are odd. Whichever the corpus picks, the alternating block excludes it. Lean: both_corpus_budgets_are_odd

assertions.name: every_corpus_proposed_gluon_count_is_even_hence_excluded
assertions.source: the corpus proposes [2, 4] gluon crossings; both are EVEN, so both leave the total ODD and both are excluded in the alternating block. This is a measured consequence of the parity theorem, not an independent finding

assertions.name: odd_dressings_are_ALL_admissible_and_even_ones_ALL_excluded
assertions.source: swept every dressing over the 3-letter alphabet at each length k = 0..5 (364 in total). At every ODD k all are admissible; at every EVEN k all are excluded; no length is mixed. So the constraint is a PARITY and not a count -- k = 1, 3 and 5 all satisfy it, and parity alone does NOT select 3

assertions.name: the_smallest_count_satisfying_BOTH_is_three_but_parity_does_not_pick_it
assertions.source: qbeta_adjunction_ilp_probe measured by INTEGER FEASIBILITY that the minimum gluon dressing is 3; parity independently requires it to be ODD. 3 is the smallest count meeting both, and 2 meets neither. 🛑 The two arguments are recorded as CONVERGING, not combined: that probe says its own predicate is 'my reading' and not established as the corpus's, and choosing 3 because two arguments intersect there would be selection against the target

assertions.name: both_corpus_nucleons_as_built_are_excluded
assertions.source: both are 11 letters and both have negative alternating character, so under scope (B) neither is admissible -- and by section 4 that is not repairable by changing WHICH letters are used, only by changing HOW MANY

description: The crossing budget must be EVEN under scope (B), because the alternating block is 1-dimensional and the character's sign is (-1)^length. The B_3 core is 6 letters (even) and the quark block 3 (odd), so admissibility turns on exactly one thing: the GLUON DRESSING must have ODD length. Proved first in Lean (gluon_dressing_must_be_odd, sorry-free). Consequences measured here: every gluon count the corpus proposes (2 and the retracted 4) is EVEN and therefore excluded; and the 9-vs-11 budget debate cannot bear on this at all, because 9 and 11 differ by 2 and so share a parity. Converges independently with qbeta_adjunction_ilp_probe's measured minimum of three gluon crossings. NOT claimed: that parity selects 3 -- any odd dressing satisfies it, and this probe checks that.

core.what: B_3 = (sigma_0 sigma_1^-1)^3, the Borromean gluon field

quark.what: the flavour crossings; THIS is where the obstruction lives

gluon.what: the dressing whose parity decides admissibility

build_nucleon_nf.note: its docstring: 'B_3 IS the gluon structure'

budgets.verdict: same parity, so the 9-vs-11 argument cannot bear on this

independent_convergence.ilp_own_caveat: 'the predicate is my reading of (G x)_gamma ... one confirmed prediction does not make it the corpus's predicate' -- so it is scope-(a), not settled
independent_convergence.relationship: INDEPENDENT arguments that agree on excluding 2. NOT combined to select 3 -- parity admits 1, 3, 5 alike

scope.invariant: the sign of the alternating character, = (-1)^length
scope.what_is_NOT_claimed: that parity selects 3, or any particular count. It excludes 2 and 4 and admits every odd count
